Grant of Restricted Shares under Long Term Incentive Plan
Tower Resources plc (AIM: TRP), the AIM listed oil and gas company focused on Africa, announces that it has made an annual award of Restricted Shares to directors, employees and consultants under its Long Term Incentive Plan ("LTIP").
The award of Restricted Shares (the "Restricted Shares"), comprising 1,540,000,000 new ordinary shares ("Ordinary Shares") in the capital of the Company, was made on 26 June 2026 and the Restricted Shares will vest only at the end of three years, on 26 June 2029. The award of equity incentives under the LTIP (the "LTIP Award") is an annual event, which normally takes place in the first quarter of each year, and has in previous years been made in the form of share options vesting over three years; however, last year the Company decided to issue Restricted Shares which only vest at the end of three years, and the Company has decided to adopt the same approach this year and going forward.
The current year's award is for the same number of shares as last year, distributed among a slightly larger group of recipients, and remains within the Company's existing policy that the cumulative amount of shares which may be issued in future under LTIP awards, whether in the form of share options or restricted shares, shall not exceed
10% of the Enlarged Share Capital of the Company, being the sum of the currently issued shares and all future shares that the Company may be currently obliged to issue in future, including restricted shares, options or other conversion rights.

latest.title: Letter of Approval for PEL96 Farm-out
latest.content:
25 Jun 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 6559J
Tower Resources PLC
25 June 2026
25 June 2026
Tower Resources plc
("Tower" or the "Company")
Namibia Update: Letter of Approval for PEL96 Farm-out
Tower Resources plc (AIM: TRP), the AIM-listed oil and gas company focused on Africa, is delighted to announce that it has received a formal letter of approval from the Namibian Ministry of Industries, Mines and Energy ("MIME") for the farm-out of the PEL96 license, offshore Namibia, to Prime Global Energies Limited ("Prime").
This represents the finalisation of the only outstanding condition precedent under the PEL96 farm-out contract, announced on 10 January 2025. The Company will now send out a notice of completion to Prime, and a draft deed of assignment, novation and amendment to MIME and Tower's partners, with completion expected to follow shortly.
The Company is still awaiting approval for the proposed purchase by its wholly owned subsidiary Tower Resources (Namibia) Limited ("TRNL") of an additional 5% interest in the PEL96 license from its local partner, ZM Fourteen Investment (Pty) Ltd ("ZM") (together, the "Parties"), announced on 7 March 2025. As a result of the delay, the Parties are no longer bound to complete the acquisition of this interest, but are continuing to discuss its execution.
Tower Resources Chairman & CEO, Jeremy Asher, commented:
"We are very pleased to have received this letter of approval, and would like to thank the relevant personnel at MIME, the Upstream Petroleum Unit and NAMCOR for their diligent review and continued engagement throughout this process. We would also like to welcome Prime, who we view as a highly favourable partner for PEL96, with substantial technical and financial resources and a track record of operational success. We look forward to working alongside them and our other stakeholders to progress with the work programme offshore Namibia."

company_30s.what_they_do: TRP Ltd is a small oil‑and‑gas exploration company that owns a handful of onshore licences in the UK.  Its core activity is drilling and developing these licences into production wells, with the goal of turning the assets into a source of revenue.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The UK has a long‑standing supply of oil and gas, and the region where TRP operates has proven reserves that many larger operators consider too small or too risky.  If TRP can secure a partner and bring the asset to production, it could tap into a market that still needs new supply and offer a foothold for future growth.
company_30s.current_state: TRP is still in the exploration phase, has not yet produced revenue, and is actively raising capital to cover its cash burn.  The company has just finished an AGM that approved a new farm‑out deal and a licence update, and it has secured a bridge loan to keep the business afloat.

rns_narrative: The AGM confirmed a farm‑out that brings in a new partner, giving the company fresh capital and a larger team to work the licences.
The company is raising subscription capital and has secured a bridge loan, showing it is actively seeking liquidity to keep drilling operations going.
Recent updates on licences and the farm‑out suggest the company is moving from a cash‑burning exploration stage toward a more structured development plan.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Silent but watchful – traders are quietly buying while the broader market remains indifferent.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls are pointing to the AGM approval of the farm‑out and the surge in buy orders as signs that smart money is stepping in.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears worry that the company still has no revenue, a high debt load, and that the farm‑out could fall through if the partner backs out.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The mood has shifted from neutral to slightly bullish as trading volume spikes and buy‑limit orders appear.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is dead, meaning no mainstream interest.  This creates the best surprise potential if a catalyst hits.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the farm‑out deal and the partner’s capital injection.
First drilling results from the newly licensed area – a hit would validate the asset.
Announcement of a definitive production plan or a production start date.
Release of the next quarterly report showing improved cash flow or a reduction in debt.
expect_next.watch_for: A sudden spike in volume at the AGM price, a positive drilling result, or a partner announcement.  These signals would confirm that the market is starting to price in the asset’s potential.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stage of a recovery after a deep sell‑off.  The APEX score indicates a tight trading range, so if support holds, a rebound is likely.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The stock sits at a deep crash bottom, and the farm‑out brings in a partner that has historically invested in similar assets.  Historical RED signals show an average return of about 160 % when the market reverts.  If the price recovers to roughly halfway between its low and the pre‑crash high, the upside is in the 100‑150 % range.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the farm‑out collapses or the company fails to secure the needed capital, the stock could continue to slide toward zero.  The worst‑case scenario is a total loss of the invested capital.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside 2–3 × the entry price versus a downside that can only take the position to zero.  The asymmetry is strongly in favor of a rebound if the catalyst materialises.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price holds above the AGM support level and volume spikes.  Allocate about 10 % of the portfolio, use a stop 10 % below entry to protect against a false break, and stay in the trade until the price breaks the top of the tight range.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a confirmed drilling result or a partner announcement.  If volume rises 1.5‑2 × the average and the price breaks the upper support, consider a small entry.
playbook.if_passing: None identified – the company is not delisting or filing for bankruptcy, so a contrarian bullish stance remains justified.

ai_insights.bottom_line: A deep crash bottom coupled with a fresh farm‑out and a silent market signals a high‑asymmetry rebound is likely, provided the partner capital and drilling results materialise.
